name: 시 낭독 리허설
prompt:
Cinematic progressive pencil-and-ink line animation on a solid pure bright white background, edge to edge. The very first frame is an entirely empty white field. Static locked-off camera, one continuous 8-second take.

The subjects: a master poet demonstrating expressive posture at one side of a small amphitheater stage, a performance coach guiding a nervous young poet through the same gesture, an invited guest listening from the foremost seat, a theater guard half-visible beside a velvet curtain cropped by the right edge, and a vast ascending sweep of empty seats rising behind the group.

0-3.5s: delicate light-graphite pencil strokes are traced visibly from endpoint to endpoint — soft, feather-light, barely pressed, like an artist's first gentle sketch, each line drawn once. No dense cross-hatching, no engraving-style shading; only airy contour lines. The large landscape forms are drawn first with rich observational detail, the main subject last, in a few precise strokes. The composition is asymmetric — the main subject sits off-center. Built progressively, never fading in.

3.5-5.5s: pale watercolor tints rise FROM INSIDE the pencil lines, within the lines — a restrained palette of mulberry on the stage curtain, peacock blue on the coach's jacket, warm honey gold on the wooden stage and empty seats, and soft jade on the guest's scarf, each heavily diluted with water. The larger the area, the lighter and more watery its wash — broad fields, hills and skies receive only the palest, water-flooded tint, far lighter than the small subjects. Color blooms ONLY onto the drawn subjects — all surrounding space stays pure untouched white. The delicate pencil drawing remains the protagonist; color is only a light stain resting on the lines. Generous areas of the paper stay untouched white, and the painting dissolves into untouched white paper well before the frame — soft, wet watercolor boundaries, with generous white margins breathing on at least three sides of the image. One consistent light direction with soft believable shadows. The white background stays pure white. The sky, when present, stays essentially untouched white paper — only the palest breath of tint near the horizon and a few light pencil cloud outlines, never a fully painted sky.
5.5-8s: the young poet lifts the chin and opens both arms into the coached pose while the master poet answers with a precise encouraging nod; a warm rehearsal light grows across the stage boards and reaches the guest's front-row seat. Everything else stays perfectly still.

Style: delicate pencil-and-ink drawing with airy line weight and rich observational detail, fresh luminous watercolor, clear summer daylight, cinematic depth of foreground, middle ground and far horizon — the feel of a beautiful illustrated atlas for curious teenagers, never a kindergarten picture book. Museum-quality contemporary illustration.

Never: text, letters, numbers, hashtags, watermarks, a visible drawing hand, pen, pencil or brush in frame, primary crayon colors, muted grey or slate mood, sepia, ink-wash painting mood, fog, smiling sun, V-shaped birds, rainbows, dense cross-hatching, engraving-style shading, heavy dark outlines, dead-center composition, paint splatter, color outside the lines, paper texture, visible paper grain, window light streaks, ambient room shadows, vignette, camera movement, cuts, dissolve.
